clue.text: Suit covered in salt sent back to be repaired

indicators.note: sent back tells you the whole assembled run of letters is read from its far end
covered in puts the word for suit inside the word for salt

parts.note: salt spread on winter roads is a de-icer
to suit is to fit, as in a job that suits you

explanation.surface: A salt-stained suit has been posted back to the tailor for mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' builds DEIFITCER, which 'sent back' turns round as one run. Salt here is the grit spread on icy roads, not table salt or a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something put right or mended has been fixed.

clue.text: Chicken or duck in a roll

indicators.note: in places the duck's letter inside the word for a roll

parts.note: a roll is a list of names, as is a roster
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, written O

explanation.surface: A lunch choice between two kinds of poultry served in a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts O inside ROSTER. A duck is cricket's word for a batsman's score of zero, and the roll is a register of names rather than bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cockerel is a male domestic fowl.

parts.note: around is circa, abbreviated c before dates
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A dog's leash looped round some padlocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' is a verb here, as in presiding over a meeting, and the locks are on a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to preside over a meeting is to head it.

clue.text: Opening of cage after funny line — it's a stiff!

indicators.note: after says the letter from cage follows the rearranged letters
funny in the sense of odd, so the letters next to it are put in an odd order
opening of takes the letter that starts the word cage

explanation.surface: A comedian's gag falls flat just as the cage door opens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges LINEITSA into INELASTI, and 'after' puts the C from 'Opening of' cage on the end. A stiff in the surface is a corpse or a flop; here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: material that will not stretch or give is rigid.

parts.note: the printed word is a slip: change its L to a T and split it after the first letter and you get the phrase a speaker says when put right

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a deliberate misprint. Put right the wrong letter in 'Island' and you have the first two words of the answer; the third word says what you just did.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: both are what you say on admitting a mistake.

clue.text: Relief for Australian when mounting copy

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in a down entry each piece is read from the bottom up

parts.note: relief sent to a disaster zone is aid
Oz is informal for Australia or Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian gets some respite while putting a print into a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mounting' turns each piece upwards: AID becomes DIA and OZ becomes ZO. Relief for an Australian is 'Oz aid', read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a kind of photocopy made by a dye-line process.

indicators.note: all over has the fish covering the lake's letter on both sides

parts.note: a cod is a common sea fish
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Lifeless fish are floating everywhere on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' puts COD around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a body that has lost its warmth is lifeless.

clue.text: Problem at the address of sister's house

parts.note: c/o, care of, is written on a letter sent to someone at another's address
a sister in a convent is a nun
drum is British slang for a house or flat

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong at the place where a sibling lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drum' is British slang, originally underworld, for someone's home. The sister is a religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a puzzle or riddle that is hard to resolve.

clue.text: Fifty nuts in a cut fruitcake

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the three words after it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A slice of rich cake turns out to contain fifty nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges INACUT into UNATIC after the Roman L. Fruitcake is slang for a mad person, not something from a bakery.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both are informal words for a crazy person.

parts.note: a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A grateful poet donates their home to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: he was a Roman writer of odes and satires.

clue.text: End of bit coming down drill

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of the word bit

parts.note: when rain is coming down it is raining

explanation.surface: The tip of a drill bit descends into the work.
explanation.walkthrough: Bit and drill suggest a power tool, but the drill is the practice kind, as in military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: repeated practice or instruction is exercise.

indicators.note: form of says the two chemical words appear in another shape, their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist finds a nitrate compound nobody has identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges ORGANICNITRATE. 'Unknown' is a noun here, as in a venture into the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin phrase for unexplored territory, used for any unfamiliar subject.

clue.text: Supply lines for start of military exercise

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pro and con

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of the word military

parts.note: PT is physical training, the school and army name for exercise

explanation.surface: Logistics routes are laid out before army manoeuvres begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is a verb and the lines are an actor's: giving them from the wings is the definition. PT is the British school and forces abbreviation for physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre sense: to feed an actor forgotten words from the wings.

clue.text: The end of it is — in this

definitions.text: The end of it is — in this

parts.words: The end of it is — in this
parts.note: the word 'it' finishes with T, and the printed dash is exactly how that letter is signalled in the telegraph alphabet of dots and dashes

explanation.definitionFit: Literal description: T is sent as a single dash in the telegraph alphabet.

definitions.meaning: to get an illness is to catch it
a bargain is an agreement or deal struck between two parties

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to catch a disease, and a formal agreement or deal.

indicators.note: in places the river and the mole together inside the word for simple

parts.note: a simple, unworldly person is naive
R is the map abbreviation for river
a mole, a traitor who informs from inside, is a rat

explanation.surface: A children's tale about a mole living on a riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, not part of the story. The mole is a spy who betrays, not the burrowing animal of the riverbank tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an account of events, a tale.

clue.text: Road menace obviously gutted if trapped by strong drink

indicators.note: trapped by says the strong drink closes around the two letters left from obviously

parts.note: a bracer is a stiff drink taken to steady the nerves

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides of obviously, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dangerous driver is clearly devastated at being caught over the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' and 'if trapped by' are the signals; in the surface they read as upset and arrested. The answer is British slang for a young man who drives fast and recklessly in a souped-up car.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a youth who drives dangerously fast.

clue.text: To have an object that the opposition may thank you for?

definitions.text: that the opposition may thank you for?

parts.note: to have something is to possess it
an object is an aim or purpose, as in the object of the exercise

explanation.surface: Possessing some item that your rivals would be grateful for.
explanation.walkthrough: The object is an aim, not a thing. In football the answer is a score put into your own side's net.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunder that scores for the other side, so a gift to your opponents.

clue.text: Chap, apparently owing money, put away

indicators.note: apparently says the chap looks as if he owes money, which is to be 'in' the colour of debt, so his word goes inside it

parts.note: an account that owes money is in the red
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow who seems to be in debt has been locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' asks you to picture the chap as 'in the red', the bookkeeping phrase for being in debt, and to take that picture literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to send an accused person into custody before trial is to lock them up.

parts.note: November is N in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: riots means runs wild, so the letters of the county's name are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A news headline dated the ninth of November about unrest in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' points to the answer at 9 across, TRAINING, which is the definition. 'riots' rearranges SURREY, an English county south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a learner's practice ground, as in the gentle ski slopes for beginners.

definitions.note: a lot is an item in an auction; the question mark admits the definition says where such an item is, not what it is

indicators.note: the answer at 7 down means crazy, which tells you the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the answer at 17 across, REMAND, is used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Two numbers and a complaint that someone caused great pain.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' stands for LUNATIC, the anagram signal, and '17' for REMAND; with 'he hurt me' that makes REMANDHEHURTME, rearranged. 'a lot' is an auction item, not a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for being up for sale at auction, the state of an item being bid on.

definitions.meaning: a light blanket or rug draped over a sofa or bed
to hurl an opponent to the ground, as a wrestler or judo player does

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a light cover draped over furniture, and to hurl a wrestling opponent down.

indicators.note: into sends the turned word inside the synonym for the answer at 7 down

parts.note: the answer at 7 down is LUNATIC, a synonym of mad

indicators.note: turning means the word by is read from its last letter to its first

explanation.surface: A sum in which four is somehow converted into seven.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' is the answer at 4 down, an apology, and is the definition. 'turning' makes YB, and 'into' places it within a synonym of the answer at 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal equivalent: both are ways of admitting a mistake was yours.

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word after it, from
animated means set in motion, so the letters of the word beside it move about

explanation.surface: A tyrant who turns out to be a character from an animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes M from 'from', and 'animated' rearranges CARTOON into ONOCRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ruler who holds power alone.

parts.note: to be part of a group is to be in it
B is black on pencils and in chess notation
cherry is a shade of red

explanation.surface: The unprocessed portion of a dark cherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' looks like a signal that the answer sits inside the next words; instead it supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a quality that is innate, present from birth.

indicators.note: sound from says the answer is what you hear when the word for bolted is spoken

parts.note: someone who bolted ran off fast: they flew

explanation.surface: A noise comes from a mine shaft that has been secured shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound from' makes FLEW, said out loud, into the answer. Bolted means ran away, not fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chimney duct that carries smoke upward.

clue.text: Unite? Yes, and break up midweek

parts.note: to unite two people in marriage is to wed them

indicators.note: break up tells you the letters of the two words before it are broken apart and reset

explanation.surface: A trade union votes to join forces and take a break in the middle of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break up' rearranges YESAND into NESDAY. Unite is also the name of a large British trade union, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: The day in the middle of the working week.
